events.title: Germantown Is Founded in Pennsylvania
events.description: German immigrants, many of them Quakers and Mennonites, founded Germantown in the Pennsylvania Colony. It became the first permanent German settlement in North America.
events.significance: Germantown became a gateway for German immigration to America. In 1688 its residents also issued one of the earliest organized protests against slavery in the colonies.

events.title: 'The Jazz Singer' Premieres
events.description: Warner Bros. opened The Jazz Singer, starring Al Jolson. It was the first prominent feature film to combine synchronized singing and speech with its story.
events.significance: Its success showed that audiences wanted sound in movies. Within a few years the silent-film era was effectively over.

events.title: The Yom Kippur War Begins
events.description: Egyptian forces crossed the Suez Canal and attacked Israeli positions on the Bar Lev Line in the Sinai Peninsula. Syria launched a coordinated attack at the same time, and the Yom Kippur War began.
events.significance: The war shook Middle East politics and set off an oil crisis. It also opened the way to later diplomacy, including the Egypt-Israel peace process.
